planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average to poor, well-drained soil in full sun; Sheila McQueen's brighter chartreuse foliage sets it apart from the gray-green leaves of most border sedums.

directions: Grow in lean to average, sharply drained soil in full sun; like other upright sedums, Sheila McQueen declines quickly in wet or overly rich ground that causes weak, floppy growth. This older British heritage selection is valued for its unusually bright, yellowish-green foliage, a noticeably chartreuse tone rather than the gray-green or blue-green of most telephium-type sedums, which glows against the broad, flat heads of reddish-pink flowers that open in late summer. Though never patented itself, it has become an important parent in modern sedum breeding, passing its distinctive coloring and vigor into newer introductions such as the citron-flowered 'Lemonjade'. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain a tidy, upright habit.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 10-12 weeks before last frost, or plant purchased transplants after frost danger passes; Lascar is a seed-grown verbena series bred for early flowering and a tidy mounded-trailing habit.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; Lascar is a seed-raised breeding line developed to flower earlier and more uniformly than older garden verbena, with a compact, mounded-trailing habit and full, well-filled centers that avoid the bare middles common in older trailing selections. It is offered across a wide range of solid and eyed colors spanning white, pink, red, purple, and burgundy tones, all blooming continuously from planting through frost with minimal deadheading. Good resistance to powdery mildew keeps foliage clean through humid Gulf South summers that cause older seed-grown verbena to decline by midsummer. Its medium vigor and moderate spread make it well suited to hanging baskets, mixed combination containers, and smaller bedding schemes where a less aggressive trailing habit than vegetative series like Superbena is preferred.

common_name: Obsession Verbena (Compact Early-Flowering Seed Verbena Series)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 10-12 weeks before last frost, or plant purchased transplants after frost danger passes; Obsession is a compact, strongly branching seed verbena series bred to finish earlier than most other seed-grown verbena.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Obsession is a seed-grown verbena series bred by PanAmerican Seed for a low, dense, strongly branching habit with naturally short internodes, giving compact, well-proportioned plants without growth regulator treatments. It is notably faster to flower than most other seed verbena, finishing in around 11-14 weeks depending on container size, and is offered in an unusually broad palette of more than a dozen solid and contrasting-eyed colors from white and apricot through burgundy and scarlet. Plants bloom continuously from spring through frost with only light grooming needed to keep them tidy, tolerating heat and short dry spells well once established. Its small, uniform scale makes it especially well suited to compact bedding schemes, mixed six-packs, and smaller container combinations where taller or more sprawling verbena selections would overwhelm the design.
